fatal_errors: The proposed DFT-based intervention does not reconstruct the experimental HEBM-plus-SPS method.
The hypothesis omits the CoCrFeNiTi composition and all decisive milling and sintering conditions.
DFT simulations cannot directly refine or densify a microstructure; they can only help predict or guide processing and phase selection.
The claimed percentage improvements are invented and unsupported by evidence.
Microstructure refinement is incorrectly associated with an increase in grain size.
The predicted properties and phases do not match the reported 675 Hv hardness, 1894 MPa compressive strength, 1238 MPa yield stress, or 83% FCC/17% BCC structure.
explanation: The response recognizes the broad goals of phase stability and property optimization but substitutes a generic computational workflow for the target powder-metallurgy process. It misses high-energy ball milling, spark plasma sintering, their processing windows, nanocrystalline grain refinement, densification, FCC/BCC stabilization, and the Hall-Petch, dislocation, and solid-solution strengthening mechanisms. Its baseline and boundary conditions are unrelated to the target, and its quantitative claims have no cited or supplied evidence. The proposed comparison is only weakly falsifiable because trial-and-error is not standardized and no specific alloy, process, or computational-to-experimental linkage is defined.
